viewer_sees: A stonecutter chisels rows of small incised characters into a tall grey rock face while a robed emperor in gold ornaments stands a few paces off, arms folded, watching the chips fly
Ashoka sits enthroned in a pillared timber-and-stone hall of Pataliputra, courtiers and fan-bearers along the walls, a carved lion-footed throne, sunlight slanting through latticed windows
Centuries later, a monk-scribe in an oil-lit monastery cell writes slowly on a palm-leaf manuscript while a faded painted mural of a fierce king on the wall behind him flickers in the lamplight
A polished stone pillar stands alone in an open field at dawn, rows of carved lines running down its face; the camera glides slowly toward the carving as the first light crosses it

ANIMATED MAP — on a cream parchment the eastern coast of India: coastal trade routes draw themselves along the shore around one shaded kingdom, then the colour of the Mauryan lands floods across it as army markers advance
A broad river plain at dawn lies under thick mist; nothing can be made out in it, only a few pale tree crowns and the glint of the river, as the mist slowly drifts and closes again
Close on a stonecutter's hands driving a chisel into a rock face, fresh chips flying, a line of carved characters growing under the mallet
CROWD-AS-TEXTURE — a long slow column of deported people walks along a red dust road away from the camera, smoke rising from burned villages on the far horizon, no individual faces
A chisel and wooden mallet rest on a stone ledge beside freshly cut columns of tally strokes; dust sifts down the rock face and no other hand is in the frame
Ashoka stands alone on a ridge at dusk, looking over a wide darkening plain, the red light fading from his face and robes as the wind lifts his cloak
Ashoka sits alone on the floor of a lamplit chamber, a saffron-robed monk's low voice unseen, his hands open on his knees and his head slowly lifting toward the flame
Close on Ashoka's face in flickering lamplight, eyes lowered, his jaw working, one hand rising slowly to cover his mouth

A peaceful Kalingan village under a banyan tree where an ascetic teaches a few seated villagers; then a man and woman walk apart down a road, looking back over their shoulders toward each other as guards stand between them
MACRO OBJECT — Ashoka's open hand holds a pinch of red earth, and the grains fall one by one through his fingers until only a few remain on his palm
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION — a vast royal kitchen, rows upon rows of great bronze cauldrons over fires and cooks hauling pots, the rows stretching on and on
In the quiet kitchen courtyard two peacocks and one deer stand together on swept stone beside an open doorway, a cook with a bowl looking at them
A dusty road lined with newly planted saplings and a stepped well where workers lower pots, while a healer in a plain wrap tends the leg of a bullock by the roadside
Ashoka eats from a low platter on a mat in a lamplit room when a breathless messenger kneels in the doorway with a scroll and he raises his hand to let him speak
A heavy wooden prison gate stands open as an officer in a plain tunic leads an elderly man out into the light, where a woman waits with her hands joined
CROWD-AS-TEXTURE — seen from above, the Mauryan army massed on a plain in tight ranks of infantry, war elephants and chariots, dust rising, one banner line moving across the whole formation
At a forest edge a Mauryan officer with armed soldiers faces a group of forest-dwelling people with bows and leaf-and-cotton wraps, the officer raising one firm hand
MACRO OBJECT — a sheathed sword lies on a folded cloth beside a carved stone wheel, a thin ribbon of incense smoke curling up between them

ANIMATED MAP — on a parchment, thin lines of envoys and monks travel out from India westward across deserts to five marked Greek kingdoms, then southward to the Tamil lands, dots lighting up along each line
Ashoka and two grown sons stand before a freshly carved stone; Ashoka rests a hand on it and the young men look at it gravely
A long road crosses a wide landscape of hills, river and plain, and polished stone pillars rise at intervals along it, each in a different terrain, as the camera sweeps along
Beside the Kalinga coast a granite hillock with a carved stone elephant rising from its rock; Mauryan officers stand before the rock face, looking up at it
A royal reader stands before the rock addressing a row of seated Mauryan officers; the officers listen, one frowning, one lowering his eyes
Ashoka stands on a low dais before gathered Kalingan elders, his lips closed and hands joined behind his back; a blank stone slab beside him waits uncarved
A lone rider on a long road crosses sand dunes toward a far frontier town, a scroll case at his saddle, a stone pillar at the roadside and endless sand beyond
TIMELINE/SEASONS — one fixed view of a pillar in a field: seasons turn, moss and vines creep up the carved letters, village rooftops appear and change, until the writing is hidden
Monks in saffron robes chant before a white domed stupa at dusk, oil lamps lit along its base

Hundreds of men haul a massive stone pillar lying on a huge wheeled cart with thick ropes toward a river while a sultan on horseback watches; then Brahmin scholars gather around the pillar, one shaking his head
In an 1830s study in Calcutta a British scholar at a desk piled with ink rubbings of carved letters compares one sheet to another, a pundit beside him pointing, a lamp lit
Ashoka stands alone under an open sky, face tilted upward toward the light, cranes crossing above him; nothing identifies him in the frame
The four-lion capital on top of a polished pillar at dawn, the stone lions facing four ways and gold light on their manes
EMPTY AFTERMATH — a wide view of the Kalinga hillside with green fields and a river below and a bare smooth rock face with no carving on it, the wind moving the grass
END CARD
